somaschi_2016.title: Near optimal single photon sources in the solid state
assumptions: Abstract-summary source scenario; the quoted values are not a jointly calibrated single operating point.
The body separately quotes brightness 0.16 +/- 0.02; preserve the abstract value without silently merging the two.
Finite support n<=2; independent pulses; ideal balanced optics and threshold detectors are scenario assumptions.
Published uncorrected overlap is context, not the direct two-input click-visibility target.

ding_2016.title: On-Demand Single Photons with High Extraction Efficiency and Near-Unity Indistinguishability from a Resonantly Driven Quantum Dot in a Micropillar
assumptions: Rate-budget factors: main text p. 2; rounded independent calibrations, before the added 3 GHz etalon.
HOM scenario mean is preparation*extraction; output loss is polarization*path*fiber. These are derived values.

Purity and HOM measurements use the added etalon; its throughput and full pulse interferometer are unavailable here. Combining them with the rate budget is a sensitivity scenario, not a calibrated hardware prediction.
No fit to the reported count rate or raw visibility is performed.

menssen_2017.title: Distinguishability and many-particle interference
locations: main Eqs. (4) and (14), Fig. 4 constant-modulus triad-phase protocol
assumptions: Ideal symmetric tritter formula regression; no digitized experimental count-rate fit.
Mixed-state eigenvalues 0.7 and 0.3 are selected validation inputs, not measured parameters from the paper.

ollivier_2021.title: Hong-Ou-Mandel Interference with Imperfect Single Photon Sources
ollivier_2021.role: Motivates explicitly specifying the extra-photon wavepacket. Its separable-noise approximation is not assumed to equal PLQ's conditional P(2) noise hypothesis or click normalization. No experimental reproduction is claimed.
